Most analysis projects rot because nobody can re-run them six months later.
Here's the skeleton I start every project with so that `make all` reproduces
everything from raw data to the figures in the paper.

## The layout

```
project/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/          # never edited by hand
│   └── derived/      # everything here is regenerated
├── R/                # functions, sourced not run top-to-bottom
├── analysis/         # numbered scripts: 01_clean.R, 02_model.R ...
├── figures/
├── renv.lock         # pinned R dependencies
├── Makefile
└── README.md
```

## The rule that makes it work

Raw data is read-only. Everything in `data/derived/` is produced by a script
and can be deleted and rebuilt at any time. If you can't delete it and get it
back, it doesn't belong there.

## A tiny Makefile

``` makefile
all: figures/fig1.png

data/derived/clean.rds: analysis/01_clean.R data/raw/source.csv
	Rscript $<

figures/fig1.png: analysis/02_model.R data/derived/clean.rds
	Rscript $<
```

Make only re-runs what changed. Touch the cleaning script and just the
downstream steps rebuild.
